items.summary: Savage Planet series developer Raccoon Logic announced a new game at Gamescom today, and it's not what anyone

content.v: Savage Planet series developer Raccoon Logic announced a new game at Gamescom today, and it's not what anyone would expect.
Breakaway Hockey League is a new "high-skill" 4v4 ice hockey game with five-minute matches, ranked play, and what the studio called "larger-than-life spectacle."

In development for PC, Breakaway Hockey League has players controlling just one member of the team, not the entire lineup like you might find in EA's NHL series. Raccoon Logic is promising things like realistic puck physics and "physical checking," along with other things you'd expect from a hockey game, including skill moves like dekes and picking your corners with precision shooting.

Raccoon Logic is hoping Breakaway Hockey League will lead to "highlight-reel moments" with its more arcade-y setup, which in turn people may share online. The game promises players "dramatic breakaways, clutch saves, and bone-rattling hits."

Raccoon Logic's marketing boss Hugo Agostinho said the team created Breakaway Hockey League in part because of a gap in the market with hockey games vanishing from PC. That's not totally true, as Steam is filled with hockey games like Bush League Hockey, Hoser Hockey, and Backyard Hockey '02, just to name a few. In any event, Raccoon Logic sees an opportunity for Breakaway Hockey League to stand out with its blend of "skill, speed, and violence."
"We're aiming to keep the soul of hockey while adding the purity of modern competitive action games," game director Steve Masters said.
Agostinho acknowledged that there are fantastic indie-style ice hockey games on Steam, but these do not scratch the specific itch that Breakaway Hockey League is going for.
"Growth of the game on a global scale"

Speaking to GameSpot at Gamescom, Agostinho said ice hockey continues to expand into new territories and reach more people, and Breakaway Hockey League is coming to market against that backdrop. He pointed out that a team from Florida, the Panthers, have now won back-to-back Stanley Cups, and he admitted he's feeling pretty salty about a US-based team doing so well. But it's also helping grow the game.

"The growth of the game on a global scale and then the types of audiences has also expanded significantly," he said. "We see places like Japan, China, France, Italy, all having their own hockey scenes. We have a professional hockey league for women in the PWHL. Montreal won the first cup, which is where the studio's based, so it's very exciting there."

He also pointed out how the HBO series Heated Rivalry recently helped introduce even more people to ice hockey. He said the show, along with other factors, has helped make hockey appealing to people other than the typical "hockey bro with a missing tooth."
"One of the funniest things I've heard is a lot of the fans who've gotten into hockey from Heated Rivalry ... they'll go to games and call it 'hockey boy aquarium.'"

Raccoon Logic is planning to launch Breakaway Hockey League via Steam Early Access, but before that, the studio is hosting alpha and beta playtests with a focus on "rapid iteration" as the studio develops the game alongside the community.

"We are making this not so much for like hardcore hockey fans as we are for like the Overwatch, the Valorant player, the Rocket League player, the Counter-Strike player," Agostinho said. "And a lot of our inspirations for design even actually come from shooter shooter games, and not so much sports games, which is a really cool place to start for something like this."
On-ice action

Unlike EA's NHL series, Breakaway Hockey League has players controlling just one skater, and not from a top-down presentation. Instead, the game is presented with a third-person, over-the-shoulder camera. The third-person perspective is aimed at making you "feel like an athlete" as opposed to watching a hockey broadcast, Agostinho said. Additionally, this perspective makes the game feel "more immersive," he said.
Unfortunately, no gameplay footage for Breakaway Hockey League has been released so far, but that's coming soon, the developers said.

items.title: Poppy Playtime studio reveals its next survival horror game, and this time it's co-op
items.summary: You've met the critters, now become one in Mob Entertainment's Escape From Playtime.

content.v: As a former employee of Playtime Co., you've explored the depths of its horrifying toy factory and met many of its inhabitants, including Huggy Wuggy, who just wants to hug you (to death).

Today Mob Entertainment, makers of Poppy Playtime , have announced a new game, and it's sending you back to that haunted toy factory once more—but this time you can bring some friends along. Escape from Playtime is a co-op horror game for 1-4 players and it's coming to early access on Steam. Here's the announcement trailer:

This time around you're playing "from the perspective of the cute-yet-disturbing Smiling Critters," says Mob Entertainment—the Critters being the misfit toys you meet in the original episodic (and singleplayer) Poppy Playtime.

"Tasked with scavenging materials for a mysterious building project that promises escape from the factory, players will need to work together and follow instructions from an ominous voice lurking somewhere in the shadows, all while evading the factory's most dangerous denizens," the developer says.

"Along the way, players can solve puzzles, uncover clues, scavenge tools, use hiding spots and alternate routes, and turn the factory layout to their advantage. Proximity voice chat adds another risk: communication is essential, but an irresponsible whisper can bring the mission to a brutal end."

Fans of the original horror series will see some familiar sights in the factory, but just because you've been there before doesn't mean there won't be a few surprises: "The mysterious Voice seems to be altering the factory's layout, creating procedurally generated environments that change with each run," says Mob Entertainment.

Well, a spooky factory full of mechanical horrors sounds like a great fit for co-op, so I'm not surprised Mob decided to make their next survival horror game a multiplayer experience. There's no date shown in the trailer, just that Escape from Playtime is "coming soon" to early access. Here's its home on Steam while you wait.

items.title: Rockstar Games Doubled in Size for GTA 6, Hired Real World Professionals for Fashion, Vehicles, and More
items.summary: Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for th

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/25/vintage-vice-city-pack-exclusive-looks-01-1787655039708.jpg
Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.

As part of a cover story for Dazed , Rockstar Games shared a boatload of information about Grand Theft Auto 6. In the piece, it was confirmed that Rockstar doubled in size following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2 in order to bring GTA 6 to life, with a new Los Angeles-based office being "almost solely" dedicated to working on nothing but the game's NPCs. For context, Rockstar had around 2,000 employees in 2018. That would put them at around 4,000 now. The studio has expanded a lot over the last decade by acquiring new studios in Australia, India, and the aforementioned LA office.

Rockstar's expansion doesn't exclusively encompass game developers. The company brought on other real-world professionals, such as Miami-based stylist Jillian Carr, who was hired to help create a “fashion ecosystem” that can capture the diversity in style, culture, and class necessary to give Vice City's people their distinct character.

“Vice City is built around vanity,” Carr said to the magazine. “Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly.”

Rockstar also hired racecar drivers to help with vehicle handling and 50 real street artists to design murals around the game's map. While consultants are hardly unique to this project, Carr and others are full-time employees at Rockstar and have been for years. Carr was specifically hired in 2023 and appears to be as much of the team's regular operations as anyone else.

Rockstar also revealed new gameplay details for GTA 6 , such as how eating, working out, and sleeping all impact your characters and much, much more. It's just the start of a larger bombardment of GTA 6 information, too. Rockstar will officially pull the veil off the game tomorrow in an extended look on Netflix , which is widely expected to give us a deep dive on gameplay.

Here’s something I never thought I’d say: the upcoming Call of Duty game is now available to preorder for a Nintendo console. Granted, Microsoft said it would do this, but hearing it and seeing it are two different things. The game in question is Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and the Nintendo platform is the Switch 2. Before you grab your pitchfork and torching every building in your neighborhood, it should be noted that there’s no way Modern Warfare 4 would fit on a Switch 2 game card. items.title: The Duskbloods Feels Like a Nintendo Party Game in a Bloody Wrapper
items.summary: Once you go beneath the surface of its wonderfully grotesque, unwelcoming exterior that’s right in line with F

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/wnzyrfiwlt-t80ttkxvnskn4mrykb-fbwpiwr8nztpi-1787768931367.jpg

If you’d told me two years ago that Nintendo and FromSoftware would team up on an online PvPvE Switch 2 exclusive that’s also kind of a spiritual successor to Bloodborne, my first reaction would have been, “it’s called the Switch 2??” But jokes aside, I would’ve found this collaboration hard to believe.

FromSoftware is one of the hottest devs on the planet right now, but its games rarely come to Nintendo platforms. Nintendo is publishing this game outside of Japan, and you can count all of the M-rated games the typically family-friendly company has ever published on basically two hands. Both companies also have long histories of fairly clunky online multiplayer, making the type of game they’ve gone in on together stand out even more. On paper, it’s a bizarre partnership, but after spending around eight hours with The Duskbloods network test last weekend, I totally get it now.

In IGN’s interview with FromSoftware’s Hidetaka Miyazaki , he spoke about how the deal came to be, stating that Nintendo was “very excited and receptive” to the idea from the jump. And now that I’ve played it, it’s so easy to see why folks at Nintendo thought this would be a good fit for Switch, because once you go beneath the surface of its wonderfully grotesque, unwelcoming exterior that’s right in line with FromSoftware’s house style, The Duskbloods plays so much like a classic multiplayer Nintendo game.

Before I jumped into the network test, a coworker pointed out that The Duskbloods is basically Bloodborne mixed with Kirby Air Ride’s City Trial (or Super Smash Bros. for 3DS’ Smash Run), and I can’t unsee that comparison. A bunch of players drop into a large map and have a limited amount of time to level up, find new powers, and contend with random field events, all in preparation for a final round where one player is crowned the victor.

It’s stuffed with crazy powerups and last-second comebacks, and it all revolves around a core belief that you don’t have to be the best, or even win, to still have a great time. That philosophy has fueled the best Nintendo party games like Mario Kart and Super Smash Bros. for decades, and The Duskbloods takes those concepts and brilliantly packages them in a very different, bloodstained wrapper. I only claimed victory in a single match over the whole weekend, but every time I lost the final bout or was culled before I got there, I excitedly queued right up to try again.

My favorite moment happened because of a random item I found that completely turned the tide in my favor. I don’t remember its exact name – and screenshots and video capture were disabled for the Network Test so I can’t really check – but it was essentially a pocket watch that let me add 30 seconds to the phase’s countdown timer. Nobody knew I had this power, and it was up to me to use its shock factor to the greatest effect.

I waited patiently to strike, perched high above a stake I wished to claim as my own to earn enough Virtue Points to advance to the next phase. Its current holder was defending the perimeter, but with about 10 seconds to go, they left to rack up some last-second kills. 10 seconds isn’t really enough time for someone to show up and steal those precious points, right? But 40 seconds is. I turned back time, leapt down, and stole the virtue for myself, just barely earning enough to move onto my first-ever finale. I promptly got crushed, but I didn’t care. That brief moment of triumph is what I’ll carry with me.

Despite loving Elden Ring and Nightreign, FromSoftware PvP has never been my strong suit. I play all sorts of other competitive multiplayer games, but something about FromSoftware’s methodical combat has never entirely clicked with me. So, I didn’t really expect to like The Duskbloods all that much. But apparently, Miyazaki designed The Duskbloods with a similar perspective in mind: “Personally, I am not very great at these high-intensity action games and things like PvP,” Miyazaki said. “So, at the start, the audience really is just myself while thinking about how I would go at this. Are there systems in place that I would enjoy, that cater to me as a player, not being someone who's really into that intense PvP? That's a lot of where it starts.”

Dying isn’t an enormous setback. Instead, it represents opportunity cost, burning valuable seconds you could be spending getting better, so you’re still motivated to stay alive as much as possible. But I found myself less hesitant to challenge a boss I might be underleveled for, and the whole map began to feel like my gothic playground.

Its unique ruleset also deemphasizes PvP outside of specific scenarios and zones. I was worried that I’d just be killed on sight any time I ran into another player, but getting into skirmishes outside of limited-time areas that explicitly reward you for killing others is rarely your best move.

That’s not to say there wasn’t some combination of trolls and players that just didn’t understand the objective that would kill me for seemingly no reason, and there are occasionally side objectives that do pit players against each other in unusual circumstances, but for the most part, I felt like I was left on my own to prepare for the Ritual Site’s opening. It’s in these stretches that The Duskbloods’ board game inspirations are most legible. In board games, you’re often indirectly competing with opponents for resources and victory points, only coming directly at odds with each other at certain moments, and The Duskbloods nails that dynamic.

When everyone does come together, it’s fantastic chaos. There’s a Smash Bros.-like nature in strategically waiting to strike while more powerful players duke it out, swooping in at the last second to steal the kill. The best player doesn’t always win, and if you bring in the right summon, items, and strategy, you can hold your own. There’s also a built-in rubber-banding mechanic to keep things close: Players on the bottom of the Virtue Point ladder get an attack boost when fighting someone above them.

After the clock hits zero at the end of each phase, there are a few seconds where all of my remaining competitors kind of just walk around and look at each other before the screen fades to black. It feels like the whistle just blew at halftime, and we’re taking a moment to tip our caps to the opposition before the next bloodbath begins. It’s just another reminder that The Duskbloods is a fun, friendly competition first and foremost, even if our surroundings are dismal and bleak.
For more on The Duskbloods, check out our hands-on preview from our trip to FromSoftware’s headquarters , and Michael Higham’s full interview with Hidetaka Miyazaki .

content.v: 在今晚未来游戏展活动中，《NO LAW》发布开发者访谈视频，这是一款剧情丰富的黑色电影风格第一人称赛博游戏，故事背景设定在一座霓虹闪烁却又污秽不堪的港口城市。这里充斥着罪恶而非法律，大多数人都被债务压得抬不起头，更会在某个转角被黑暗抹去存在。在欲望港中探索，夺回属于你的东西。
游戏视频：
在《NO LAW》中，你将扮演老兵格雷·哈克。他久经沙场，又深谙欲望港的生存法则。在最后一次出任务时，哈克身负重伤，几乎丢了性命，于是决定彻底告别军旅生涯，改而追寻平静的生活。然而，即使他已不再主动招惹麻烦，在某个宿命之日，麻烦还是找上了门来。
欲望港是一座颓废的赛博工业城市，这里面朝大海，背傍峭壁，草木葱茏，鱼龙混杂，各色人等个性张扬。作为进出口贸易枢纽，三教九流都汇聚于此，想要追逐自己最疯狂的梦想。这座港口没有禁区，整座城市都是你的游乐场。就把道德留在城市之外吧——上到刺破雾霭的摩天楼顶，下至令人窒息的漆黑深巷，抛开一切束缚，尽情探索这座垂直奇观。但请谨慎选择前路：当一座城市没有了法律约束，就会有许多人开始自行伸张“正义”。
《No Law》强调玩家选择将真正影响游戏世界。开发团队也提醒玩家，不要因为系统允许就肆无忌惮地杀人——因为游戏中的每一名NPC都可以被杀死，而且死亡是永久性的。
例如，如果玩家杀死了一名商店老板，那么这家商店基本就“完蛋了”，因为没有其他工作人员可以接手，商店也会因此关门。另一名开发人员进一步解释：“如果你把城市里的所有武器商人全部干掉，那么你就再也没有办法购买枪械了。”
考虑到玩家如果大规模屠杀NPC，“确实可能让自己陷入某些困境”，因此《No Law》还加入了一套保险机制。当玩家准备杀死某个关键NPC时，游戏会提前发出警告，提醒玩家一旦将对方杀死，这名NPC之后就无法再为玩家提供帮助。
《No Law》预计将于2027年登陆PC及主机平台。

items.title: Guns of Eschaton Is a Soulslike Shooter for the Genre’s Most Masochistic Fans | gamescom 2026
items.summary: Guns of Eschaton reinvents the rules of both the soulslike and the first-person shooter, making for what seems

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/guns-of-eschaton-1787582704587.jpg

It has been a long time since a soulslike truly humbled me. After a decade of playing FromSoftware’s games and their flock of imitators, I’ve earned a more-than-solid understanding of how to achieve victory without hurling a controller into the TV. It turns out there is some truth in the “soulslikes aren’t actually hard” line that the genre’s most battle-hardened fans parrot on Reddit – after you’ve mastered the fundamentals, climbing the Souls mountain isn’t quite the impossible challenge it first seems.

Guns of Eschaton isn’t your typical soulslike, though. It’s a first-person shooter set in an apocalyptic weird west, a setup that means a great deal of your third-person melee-focused muscle memory is utterly useless here. While it still adheres to the genre’s core rules – you earn level-up currency from kills, lose it when you die, have to fight tooth and nail to reach the next bonfire checkpoint, and can battle alongside a co-op ally – it has so many of its own complicated quirks that playing it feels like learning to walk all over again. Chief among the new challenges to adapt to is that most of your enemies wield ranged weapons, and so a walk through the Old South feels like dealing with Anor Londo’s army of archers all over again.

Over the course of a recent two-hour demo, I suffered through dozens of deaths on the path to understanding Guns of Eschaton’s gunpowder-heavy rethinking of the soulslike. The most important aspect is, of course, your weapon. Developer Eschatology Entertainment has recreated a number of authentic 19th-century firearms, and throughout my demo I used a six-shot single-action revolver. It’s an admirably fiddly piece of hardware; the hammer must be cocked before each pull of the trigger, and the empty shells must be ejected one-by-one before refilling the cylinder with fresh ammunition. Reloading is an excruciatingly lengthy ordeal, and getting caught in the open with six spent cartridges is a death sentence.

You can also manually rotate the cylinder to line up specific chambers, a function that becomes important when you begin to acquire bullets with special properties, such as armour piercing or more esoteric, cursed projectiles. While the demo didn’t allow me to tinker with this system in any depth, I can already see the potential of arranging a full drum of different bullets, firing them off in sequence to cause maximum pain.

What I did get a better handle on is Guns of Eschaton’s shot sequence system. While you can dispatch enemies by simply pumping lead into them, you can achieve much more efficient kills by shooting them in particular patterns. The bucked-headed Serviteur, for instance, can be quickly eliminated by blasting its left and right leg in sequence. The rifle-wielding Severed Lawman, meanwhile, must be capped in the left leg, left arm, and then the head. Your gunslinger is equipped with a book, and pulling it out while looking at one of your ragged foes will flick to the relevant page that reveals the correct sequence.

Having only been able to play for a couple of hours, I’ve yet to decide if this sequence system is a work of genius or simply much too complicated. In general, I’m very much drawn to games that radically rethink genre conventions – I adore Doom Eternal’s lock-and-key approach, and there’s an echo of id Software’s divisive design in Guns of Eschaton. Repeating enemy types makes it easy to commit sequences to memory, and each new foe introduces a one-off scramble to do field research under fire. But even on its higher difficulty levels, Doom Eternal was never quite as punishing when it comes to progress lost, and the Doom Slayer didn’t have to reload any of his weapons, never mind feed in each cartridge one at a time. And yet, the approach ensures there’s purpose in each stand-off, so much so that even “cannon fodder” enemies are combat puzzles to solve. I admire Eschatology Entertainment’s dedication to making each and every enemy feel like a duel.

Side note: there is a dedicated duel mechanic, which demands you stay perfectly still and only fire back after deflecting the enemy’s shot. But this is how almost every face-to-face shootout functions, so at least at this early stage the dueling feels a bit redundant.

Oh yeah, you can deflect bullets. Guns of Eschaton wouldn't be able to lay claim to the soulslike badge if it didn’t have a parry system, and your gunslinger’s bullet-stopping powers are a vital part of each engagement. Enemy weapons emit a flash of light and make a mechanical “chambering” sound before firing, which is your cue to perform a parry. A pair of spectral arms shield your face, and perfect timing triggers a brief window of slow-motion within which you can fire off a damaged-buffed counter-attack. As with so many melee action games, it’s a source of deep satisfaction. However, there are some frustrations that come as a result of this being a shooter – often there are multiple enemies firing at you simultaneously, and parrying plus countering all incoming attacks is a difficult exercise. Additionally, I’d often be shot at by snipers I’d not yet seen, which blindsided me with crippling damage. It felt cheap in a way Dark Souls’ surprise hidden enemies typically don’t.

In a game that already asks you to relearn many of the fundamentals of both the first-person shooter and the soulslike, there are multiple other new ideas that I was only able to briefly touch. There’s a library of abilities to be acquired from the world’s NPCs, plus a magic system with both prayers and curses, but the thing that interests me most is the bandolier worn by your protagonist. Creative director Fuad Kuliev tells me it can eventually be filled with unique handguns, each equipped with its own custom-arranged cylinder of special bullets. With multiple guns ready to go, you can fire off every round in one and then pull out the next, allowing for uninterrupted battle. It’s an approach with exciting potential – I’d love to craft a bandolier tailored to each of the game’s boss fights.

While I didn’t face any of those bosses in the demo, the trailers suggest there’s an array of fantastic-looking horrors waiting in the decaying wastes of the west. That won’t come as a surprise to those who know the name Viktor Antonov, the art director of Dishonored, Half-Life 2, Wolfenstein: The New Order, and now Guns of Eschaton. Antonov sadly passed away last year aged just 52, a tragic event that has somewhat uncomfortably become the focal point of Eschatology Entertainment’s promotional material, which constantly references that this is his final project (which is not strictly true, as Antonov also worked on the still-in-development Forest Reigns ).

The Bulgarian artist’s distinct style is clear to see in Eschaton’s world, with his bold, brutalist line work that previously created gaming’s best dystopian cityscapes now present in the frontier’s sheer cliffs and chunky details. So far I wouldn’t say it’s as striking as his work on Dishonored, in part due to the demo’s sparse desert area lacking the lived-in character that Dunwall communicates, but – as with the bosses – the trailers suggest there’s plenty of his magic in later environments.

items.title: Ubisoft Sold A Game But Forgot To Include The Literal Game Part
items.summary: Ubisoft's recent re-release of the original Heroes of Might and Magic 3 on Steam couldn't have gone much worse

content.v: Ubisoft's recent re-release of the original Heroes of Might and Magic 3 on Steam couldn't have gone much worse, as Ubisoft literally forgot to include the game files.

The arrival of the turn-based strategy classic should have been an easy win for the publisher, offering an all-time-great game, bundled alongside its two expansions, for $10 ahead of a full remake slated to arrive next year. The only issue is when players forked over the cash and installed it, they noticed the "game" was only 23.49KB in size.

As players soon discovered, Ubisoft had forgotten to include the actual game files for Heroes of Might and Magic 3. Users took to Steam's user reviews to warn others and express their disbelief. According to one user, trying to play the game instead opened a command prompt window with the text "Dummy executable ensure that you are on the right Steam branch."

As one negative user review on Steam states, "Best CMD prompt simulator of 2026. 10/10." Others continued the pile on, stating "You will own nothing and be happy," while another asked "Dude, where's my game?"
This has since been fixed to include the actual game people paid for, but according to another user review, that fix still took close to 11 hours after launch to arrive.

It won't surprise you to learn that most of the negative user reviews on Steam for the re-release are related to the snafu, with people sounding more than a little dumbstruck by how Ubisoft forgot to include the game with its game. Many are pointing prospective Steam buyers to instead purchase Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Complete on GOG , where it's currently on sale for $5. Ubisoft hasn't yet commented on the mix-up or offered an explanation.

Ubisoft will get a chance to redeem itself when it releases its full Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Remake next year. The remake will include updated 4K visuals, the original campaign, and both of the game's two expansions to tell "one unified story, enhanced with a new prologue, epilogue, and cinematic scenes."

items.title: GTA 6 leaker escalates spoilers, releases 4 minutes of Lucia's prologue
items.summary: Cyberleek wants more money.

content.v: The most anticipated game of all time continues to spring leaks. The mysterious Cyberleek , an individual who apparently has access to a build of GTA 6 and has been attempting to profit from it with a meme coin ever since, has released the biggest chunk of the game yet.

This time, it's not just joyrides and beating up random civilians: The 4 minute 38 second clip is all early Lucia story content. This is the first time Lucia, GTA 6's co-lead, has made an appearance in Cyberleek clips, which until today have focused on the other protagonist, Jason.
A message superimposed in the video reads:

"This build is actually recent and the game is not ready at all. Sony and Rockstar are killing your right to own and resell your games and Rockstar is killing their own employees too, the work required to reach gold is way too much for so little time left. Trading volume/price is how CL measures your support. CL will not continue without support. You decide."

It is certainly the most spoilery these leaks have gotten so far, and the escalation seems intentional. Cyberleek seems unsatisfied with the money they're making from the leak spree, and is doubling down on their supposedly altruistic motive while pushing their crypto. Or perhaps Cyberleek can feel the heat of Rockstar's lawyers fast approaching and hopes to squeeze more cash out of the adventure before the book is thrown in their direction.

While you should obviously avoid watching this one if you don't want to know anything about the GTA 6 story going in, I have a feeling Rockstar will reveal a lot more than this about its two main characters during the big Netflix reveal happening tomorrow.

More details about GTA 6's world and mechanics came today in the form of an early preview from youth magazine Dazed, which touched on how food and exercise will affect Jason and Lucia, how character switching works, and Rockstar's dedicated research team embedded in Miami.

items.title: Chronicles: Medieval Is Exactly as Dense and Complicated as You Thought It Would Be | gamescom 2026
items.summary: Chronicles: Medieval is one of those incredibly dense strategy games that almost immediately feels intimidatin

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/chronicles-1787707669852.jpg
Key Preview Takeaways:

Chronicles: Medieval is one of those incredibly dense strategy games that almost immediately feels intimidating to try your hand at just because of how complicated and meticulously detailed it is. Sure, sending hundreds of your Holy Roman Empire soldiers over a hill to go lay the smack down on those smarmy Frenchmen sounds great, but are you prepared to spend hours obsessing over whether or not your mercenary troops have the right weapons to deal with the heavily armored cavalry, or if your soldiers have shields big enough for them to survive a couple volleys of arrows? This historically accurate battle simulator combines elements of an RPG, an action game, and, of course, a strategy game in a way that seems specifically designed to attract those who enjoy going all the way to the bottom of the rabbit hole. That appeals to the hopeless nerd inside me, making this one I’ll definitely be keeping an eye on as it enters early access next year.

Taking place during The Hundred Years’ War, Chronicles: Medieval makes you the commander of an army for one of its three playable factions: Britain, France, and the Holy Roman Empire. As you grow your ranks, take on increasingly formidable armies, and explore the world, you’ll inevitably be drawn to large-scale Total War-style battles against rival factions, where glory or costly defeat awaits you. Historical accuracy is clearly a focus here, as any history nerd will certainly note, but developer Raw Power Games also doesn’t want that accuracy to get in the way of having fun, as they specifically shouted out when they showcased a mounted commander wielding a polearm for some reason – maybe not exactly common, but if that’s what you’re into, go for it!

The 30-minute demo I saw started in the overworld, called the Exploration map, which gives a macro view of the world – each country’s various regions and the controlling lord there (including coats of arms that are rooted in history, which is a nice touch) – but you’ll also drill down more granularly to your surrounding area as you set off on your campaign across Europe. With 209 regions, each with at least one settlement to visit and castle to storm, there seems to be quite a lot to explore, with dynamic points of interest scattered along the way, filled with things like bandit camps, mercenaries to be hired, and opportunities for trade. Naturally, you’ll also have to worry about enemy armies marching around, who might try to make a meal of your army.

And that’s where the real excitement in Chronicles: Medieval lives. Squaring off against hundreds of enemies, where you’ll need to put the full force of your various military arms to clever use by precisely positioning troops, barking out commands to adapt to the enemy’s movements, and, to give your men that extra edge they need, taking to the battlefield yourself to cut the enemy down to size. The battle that was the focus of my demo took place in continental Europe on the rolling hills of Burgundy, where our host Holy Roman Empire soldiers stared down a French company of equal size in the middle of a valley. The level of detail in this encounter was pretty impressive, as each individual soldier could be inspected, and their equipment and power level evaluated.

My favorite texture here was how troops were divided into three types: Household, Mercenary, and Levies – particularly how that difference impacted their effectiveness in battle. Household troops, who come from noble backgrounds and are the best equipped, are naturally also the most costly and difficult to train, but pay off by being highly effective in combat. Meanwhile, Mercenary troops are hired professional fighters with middling potential, while Levies, conscripted soldiers fighting because they were forced to, are down at the bottom. The main stat that determines the effectiveness of these groups is “cohesion,” which determines how well these troops work together. For example, the high-cohesion Household troops were tightly and efficiently packed together in formation and able to withstand stampeding cavalry fairly well, if properly armed for the job, while Levies were spread far apart, tended to be broken apart easily by charging enemies, and were even sometimes armed with farming equipment like pitchforks instead of real weapons of war. Seeing these disparate groups interact with one another in battle was quite fascinating to watch!

The strategy part of Chronicles: Medieval is pretty similar to something you might expect from a proper strategy/sandbox game, where you’re floating above the area and issuing commands to each part of your army individually. For example, you might want to send your cavalry ahead and flank around behind the enemy, while you send infantry forward and tell them to enter special formations like the “spearwall” that’s highly effective against mounted units. During this battle planning phase, you can augment all sorts of things with your armies as you chart out a winning strategy, like how you can thin out your men across a wider area, which gives them better coverage, but makes them more susceptible to charging enemies by spreading themselves too thin. It’s also a neat touch that, once the battle starts and the arrows start flying, you can issue additional, real-time commands, and only those units who haven’t received more specific instructions from you earlier will comply.

They also showed us the commander taking the field themselves, which transitioned things from an eye-in-the-sky view to a third-person perspective, complete with action-packed melee combat. Either on a mount, where crossing the battlefield and taking down enemies from a relatively safe distance also made it easier to bark updated orders to your men, or on foot, where it was much easier to impose your will on specific enemies that were giving your troops trouble, both of which looked like a blast.

Unfortunately, before I got to see too much of this, we did encounter a crash that abruptly shut down the demo, which is why it’s probably a good time to highlight the early access nature of this ambitious strategy game. As the first project from Raw Power Games, which is by their own account in a quite unfinished state, it will likely be a while before this lofty beast of a project doesn't have some serious rough patches. If you’re at all averse to the sometimes rocky process of playing a game before it hits 1.0, this one might be especially tough to stomach with how much it’s swinging for the fences. But if it gets there, buckle up.

items.title: New GTA 6 character swapping details revealed: Jason and Lucia can 'play as a couple, or go off and cause chaos independently'
items.summary: An interview published in Dazed magazine provides some juicy new details about GTA 6's design and development.

content.v: We've got more Grand Theft Auto 6 details to chew on, and this time not from a vegetable . An interview in magazine Dazed has revealed a bunch of details about the design of GTA 6, including how character swapping between protagonists Jason and Lucia works.
We'll get straight into it. Here are the most notable details from the interview:
1. Exercise and diet
Dazed says that food will affect Jason and Lucia's weight, and "exercising visibly builds and tones their muscles." Playing for long periods without sleeping will also impact their appearance.

Rockstar has played around with these life sims systems in past games—most recently in Red Dead Redemption 2, where Arthur could gain or lose weight based on his diet. GTA hasn't had systems this granular since 2004's GTA: San Andreas, in which CJ could gain weight and lose it through working out.
2. Character swapping

The way GTA 6 handles multiple playable characters will differ from GTA 5. The Dazed preview notes that you can "choose to either play as a couple, or go off and cause chaos independently." They described a scenario where you can cruise along the highway as Jason, then swap to Lucia in the passenger seat to "scroll on the in-game phone."
That sounds, to me, like GTA 6 will have a dynamic 'couple mode' for open world roaming—in keeping with this being a love story—but missions themselves might be solo or together.
3. Rockstar's team size

According to Dazed, Rockstar has massively expanded its team and resources to get all the details in GTA 6 right. The studio has more than doubled in size since Red Dead Redemption 2. It has an office in LA dedicated to the pedestrian NPCs that fill the open world. It also brought in over 50 real world street artists to help design the murals for GTA 6's version of Wynwood, Miami's outdoor art galleries, and there's a team of actual race car drivers handling the vehicle physics.
4. Expect to see a variety of Florida Men
Per Dazed: "Players can expect encounters with virtual iterations of Florida Man, the cultural archetype-turned-meme known IRL for wrangling alligators, drunken antics, and literal grand theft auto."
5. On music
Regarding GTA 6's music, senior vice president of narrative Ruper Humphries told Dazed:

"We love Miami music, particularly Miami bass, going through to more recent Miami artists like Kodak Black and Sexyy Red. We were also really interested in how the hip-hop scene in Miami exists in house parties in Overtown, clubs like Booby Trap on the River, and then high-end places on South Beach where bottles can cost thousands of dollars. We needed characters who could take us through those worlds."
6. Jason and Lucia's backgrounds
The preview notes that Jason is ex-military and a drug runner. Lucia is an amateur fighter (as seen in trailers) fresh out of prison.
7. Choices
Dazed suggests that player choices or behavior will affect Jason and Lucia's relationship in ways that "cut much deeper than Rockstar’s previous titles or 'honour' systems."

items.title: The Frosthaven Board Game Gets a Rare Discount on Amazon

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2023/06/06/frosthaven-blogroll-1686079848469.jpg
Update : This deal is now 100% claimed and no longer available.

Frosthaven is one of the best board games on the market. It served as a follow up to the immensely popular Gloomhaven board game, and is one of the most imposing dungeon-delving board games you can buy. It's also really quite expensive.

It's not often that we see any sort of discount on this game, but Amazon currently has a Lightning Deal running that drops it down to its lowest price ever. For a limited time (or while stock lasts), you can pick up this massive board game for $153. The discount is set to expire around 7:45pm PT or when the deal is fully claimed.

Frosthaven comes as an enormous box full of stuff. There's an incredibly thick rulebook, decks of cards, trays, dividers, a map, and miniatures. All-in-all, there are a few hundred hours worth of gameplay that comes packaged in a rather large box. And if you already own Gloomhaven characters and items, you can use them in this game as well. It's a massive campaign game that can be pretty daunting for casual players.
What We Said in Our Review
We gave Frosthaven a 9 out of 10 in our review , with the caveat that you may want to jump into Jaws of the Lion first if you're a newcomer. Here's what we had to say about the game:

"Weirdly, although Frosthaven improves on its predecessor in almost every respect, it’s far harder to recommend. Its sheer weight and the glory of the game that came before it holds it back. If you’re a Gloomhaven fan but you haven’t yet finished working your way through that behemoth of a box it’s better to stick with what you know for now rather than start a new project. If you’re new to the entire franchise then you should absolutely jump into that brilliant combat and exploration engine but the cut-down Jaws of the Lion is a better introduction. If you’re one of the rare few who not only have seen everything Gloomhaven has to offer but also remain hungry for more, however, Frosthaven is the banquet to satiate you. Bigger, bolder and better than the original, if you can find time for it in your life it’s an epic gaming experience like no other." - Matt Thrower

items.title: The Expanse’s Most Iconic Foe Shows Up In Osiris Reborn’s New Trailer
items.summary: Owlcat Games has given players a new look at its upcoming sci-fi RPG based on The Expanse. The latest trailer

content.v: Owlcat Games has given players a new look at its upcoming sci-fi RPG based on The Expanse. The latest trailer for The Expanse: Osiris Reborn aired during Gamescom 's Find Your Next Game showcase, giving players a better look at Owlcat's take on one of the TV show's most frightening foes: Project Caliban .

In The Expanse TV show (and the books upon which it is based), Project Caliban is a top-secret experiment run by a company called Protogen, which hopes to harness the recently discovered Protomolecule to create supersoldiers. Unsurprisingly, the results are tragic—and terrifying. Based on the trailer, Osiris Reborn players will be facing off with both Protogen's hired guns and one of Project Caliban's many unfortunate human test subjects, who has taken the form of a human-Protomolecule hybrid, just like the one shown in Season 2 of The Expanse TV show.

When it comes to the Protomolecule's appearance, it seems that Owlcat is taking inspiration from the television show rather than the book series--in the show, the Protomolecule is a bright, glowing blue; in the books it's described as a slimy, brownish substance rather than the bioluminescent blue seen in the latest Osiris Reborn trailer.

The new trailer also provides a better look at a female version of the player-character (simply called "the Captain" in-game) as she explores the Protogen facility on Ganymede. Osiris Reborn players can also choose to play as a male character, but after complaints about the original male player-character's voice acting surfaced in the wake of the game's April 2026 beta test, Owlcat Games has recast the role of the male lead (which is likely why we don't hear a word from him in this trailer).

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn does not yet have a specific release date, but is expected to launch for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S sometime in Q2 2027. It is currently available to wishlist on Steam .

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More
items.summary: Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is e

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/26/gta-6-raul-1787763525044.jpg
Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-type style this time around.

As part of a cover story for Dazed magazine , Rockstar Games revealed heaps of new information about Grand Theft Auto 6. Arguably the most notable details revolve around some of its gameplay features. In GTA 6, players will be able to eat, work out, and sleep, all of which have an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Players will have to take care of the Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple, as eating will affect their weight, working out will visibly change their build and strength, and a lack of sleep will negatively impact their features. It's unclear if a lack of sleep will impact the actual gameplay, or if they'll just look sleep-deprived, but it's a clear sign of Rockstar's attention to detail.

For many, this may remind them of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. That game featured a lot of RPG mechanics that allowed CJ to fluctuate in weight and fitness. Later games largely dropped these elements, but GTA 5 featured a stat system that allowed players to enhance their stamina and strength by doing physical activities such as running, playing sports, and riding bikes.

Additionally, there is also a social media feed for players to scroll, something fans have speculated about since the game's reveal in 2023. Character switching is also returning from GTA 5, allowing players to play as a couple or split up and operate independently. Dazed teased that the relationship between these two is a major focus of the game and that choices made by the player have "repercussions that cut much deeper" than the honor system in the Red Dead Redemption series.

“We look back at our previous games with a critical eye and see where we want to evolve based on what we didn’t do as well as we would have liked to, either because we didn’t have the time, resources or technological capabilities, or in some cases things we just didn’t do as well or consider as fully as we could have,” said Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. “A lot of what we do is very iterative — we adjust a lot of things by feel based on what is working and what isn’t.”

Based on that information, it's possible that there will be some kind of relationship meter that can impact how Jason and Lucia feel about each other. Ultimately, it sounds like Rockstar is making a much more nuanced and interactive game. That should hardly come as a surprise following Red Dead Redemption 2, but it seems like Rockstar is really pushing the envelope with GTA 6. Tomorrow, fans will get a proper look at the game thanks to an extended look releasing on Netflix at 3 PM ET , with a YouTube version to follow six hours later.

GTA 6 has suffered from a plethora of leaks over the last week, including a story-focused one earlier today . Rockstar Games released a statement this morning confirming that the situation was "heartbreaking," but it is working hard to deliver a product that exceeds expectations.
Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19th for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.summary: Legendary actor Tim Curry has died, aged 80. The star of the Rocky Horror Picture Show, the English actor was

content.v: Legendary actor Tim Curry has died, aged 80. The star of the Rocky Horror Picture Show, the English actor was also celebrated for his work in the recording booth, bringing dozens of animated series and video game characters to life-- including a scene-stealing performance as Premier Anatoly Cherdenko in Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3.

While a cause of death hasn't been revealed, it is worth noting that Curry had been battling various health issues after he had a major stroke in 2012. The English actor dealt with short-term memory and mobility issues following this, although he continued to work in the entertainment industry.

Film roles like Darkness in Legend, the concierge in Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, Pennywise in Stephen King's It, and Long John Silver in Muppet Treasure Island cemented his role as a Hollywood legend, and he was also a regular on several TV series throughout the decades. Curry regularly appeared on stage--including a memorable performance as King Arthur in Spamalot--and he even released several albums.
For many fans, Curry will be forever immortalized for his plans to escape to the one place uncorrupted by capitalism: SPACE!

Curry's death is sadly the latest in the entertainment industry, as country singer Dolly Parton also passed away this week, and last week, Nashville star Hayden Panettiere's death sent shockwaves when it was announced.

items.title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws'
items.summary: Everything about the studio's new game is different.

content.v: If you watched the Nodusfall trailer during Gamescom's Opening Night Live and, like me, thought the combo of Elden Ring's aesthetic and Monster Hunter's fights sounded awesome, but were worried about selling your soul to the god of gacha, fret not!
Nodusfall isn't just a visual departure for HoYoverse, swapping the vibrant anime aesthetic for something gloomier, it also represents a (partial) change in business model.

According to the devs, "Nodusfall will be a free-to-play, long-term game. What we can share at this time is that characters are not obtained through random draws. We hope to allow players to unlock this core gameplay experience through continued play. Cosmetic monetization is an important avenue we will be considering."

In my hands-on, the four available characters could be customised with different outfits, hairstyles and accessories, and I can imagine folk dropping some cash on some new fits for their boss-slaying crew, but it's a relief to know that I won't need to go through RNG hell or wipe out my bank account just to play as a surly warrior who can transform into a dual-wielding giant.

Gamescom is absolutely full of the typical anime cast gacha games this year, so it's a pleasant surprise to see the studio best known for them trying something a wee bit different. It feels different, too. Not like Genshin or Zenless Zone Zero, but not exactly like Elden Ring or Monster Hunter, despite them both being obvious inspirations. The fights are a bit more forgiving, for one, and also snappier and more fast-paced.

I've only just finished sending a trio of bosses back to whatever afterlife they go to, so I've still gotta digest what I played, but Nodusfall definitely makes a great first impression. Check back in the next couple of days for my full hands-on preview.

items.title: I added a gang notoriety system to GTA 5, but it mostly seems to make them murder everyone except me
items.summary: Which, you know, is positive I guess.

content.v: It's kind of strange that the state monopoly on violence is the only gang you can start an even slightly lasting beef with in Grand Theft Auto 5. Real-life gangs aren't known for their live-and-let-live attitude, and yet if you stroll around town shooting Ballas and Cartel members, they will adopt a stance of Christ-like forgiveness the second you're out of eyesight. The cops at least will spend a little time hunting you before they give up.

This is what I aimed to fix when I installed Gang Notoriety into my tottering Jenga tower of GTA 5 mods. The pitch is simple: gangs will get sustainably angry with you now, accruing wanted stars much like the cops do until you manage to lose the heat.
To test this new facet of GTA 5's rich simulation, I teleported (I can teleport now) to Grove Street and began shooting.

It sort of worked? The minimap blossomed with a thousand red and orange rings—each denoting a gang member who was very cross with me and ready to do something about it. I got a wanted star, too. Whether that was the gang's wanted star or just regular cops being upset about me shooting people in the street? Hard to say.

But things quickly got weird. Before too long, the assembled Ballas of Grove Street started to lose interest in me and started to gain interest in… each other? They ducked behind cover and started attacking each other, and at some point one loosed a rottweiler, which just seemed rather confused by the entire situation. Meanwhile, the frictionless vehicles of Los Santos continued to wheel all about us, including in the sky.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TEg7PusxN4bENho7hEDX8C.gif

Though my minimap was still red, everyone had lost interest in me. The Ballas seemed to have become notorious among the Ballas. They all eventually took care of themselves, save the sole survivor, who had quite the wanted level himself, thanks to a previous mod.
I will get back to you when I figure out the moral of this story.

items.title: God help us, they overclocked Mega Man
items.summary: That's going to void a warranty for sure.

content.v: Even if Mega Man's been out of Capcom's spotlight for a few years now, there's still been something refreshingly reliable about his presence. Sure, he might get a leaf shield or a throwing saw sometimes depending on which of his machine-kin he's forced to cull, but by and large, his capabilities are easy to wrap your hand around: He has an arm cannon, and you can charge it. It's predictable. It's safe. It's comfortable.
So what the hell is that?
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GAb8M8hQT4it8VYKvmGbCb.png

During last night's Gamescom Opening Night Live, Capcom released its first glimpse of gameplay for Mega Man: Dual Override, the first entry in the classic Mega Man lineup since 2018. And it's with the appropriate gravity that I'm forced to report: They've gone and overclocked Mega Man.

According to Capcom, Dual Override has Mega Man "overriding his limits and powering up for a new adventure" by using "new Custom Chips to freely modify and enhance your abilities" and an Override system that can "unleash overwhelming power for a limited time." In other words, someone thought it would be a good idea to crank up the voltage on our sweet android son beyond the recommended manufacturer guidelines.

The results, I'll admit, seem pretty effective: In the gameplay trailer embedded above, Mega Man's aftermarket mods can let him shoot a barrage of damaging projectiles, hover over platforming hazards, and dash around enemies for a more advantageous shooting position.

I can't help but notice, however, that after deploying those modifications, he's forced to expose his visibly incandescent heatsinks to avoid overheating. There's even a moment late in the footage where he pulls a Unicorn Gundam and enters Destroy Mode, exposing all his available cooling surfaces to fire a massively overcharged shot that—to his credit—insta-KOs a boss. But it also leaves him sparking and billowing smoke.
This just seems irresponsible during a hardware shortage crisis, is all I'm saying.
We don't have a precise release date for Mega Man: Dual Override yet, but it's set to launch sometime in 2027. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

items.title: 6 indie.io Games Coming to gamescom and PAX West That Have Free Demos on Steam

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-key-art-1787604509317.png

Publishing platform indie.io will be on hand at gamescom and PAX West in the coming weeks, and it’s bringing six games for people to try out in person. But if you’re not one of the lucky people who can be there yourself, don’t worry: all six games have free demos you can play on Steam right now, no badge or ticket required.

As tends to be the case with indie.io, their selection of games covers a wide range of genres. There’s everything from a cozy vineyard château builder to a brutal turn-based roguelite RPG. There’s a little something for all kinds of gamers, and you can try out all of them right now.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-key-art-1787602371901.png
Monster Park Tycoon

If you watched IGN’s recent Indie Loop showcase, you would have seen this game under another name. Formerly called Monster Zoo Tycoon, it unveiled its new name on August 10, but the dev team and core gameplay remain the same. In Monster Park Tycoon from developer OverPowered Team, you build and manage a monster park where visitors can come see a variety of strange and terrifying abominations. But there’s a twist: your park is a front for a cult. Not a very smart cult, at that.

In order to expand your park, you’ll need to trick and capture your guests using traps disguised as park props. Once you’ve got them, you can either feed them to your monsters, brainwash them to turn them into cultists, or sacrifice them to gain Faith and unlock favors from your Dark Lord.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/monster-park-tycoon-screenshot-1787602371901.jpg

Different monsters require different diets (like brains, blood, or souls), conditions for their exhibits, and behaviors that can become an issue if you ignore them. As your number of monsters grows, it’s inevitable that some of them will break free of their confinement, which is when all hell breaks loose. So you’ll have to control the chaos as you try to grow both your park and your cult in this darkly funny management sim.
Monster Park Tycoon has a brand-new demo available on Steam that marks the first time anyone outside the dev team has been able to play it.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/dunebound-tactics-key-art-1787602371900.png
Dunebound Tactics

In this roguelite, you’ll engage in tactical turn-based combat as you try to lead a band of survivors across a perilous desert in search of a new home. Your ship is fragile and your access to an all-important resource called Elios is limited. As you travel across the dunes, you’ll gather Elios from quests, from the bodies of defeated enemies, or if things get truly desperate, from sacrificing your crew members.

This is a roguelite, so you’re expected to fail. A lot. But each run builds on the ones before it. Each time a caravan is destroyed, you’ll start again with a new one. But you can find the wreck of the previous caravan, which can reward you with modules to empower your crew or even survivors who were part of your previous run.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/dunebound-tactics-screenshot-1787602371900.png

Your crew has a roster of 15 classes with 16 unique traits that determine their skills, stats, and abilities. Combat takes place on a grid, where cover is available but the terrain is fully destructible. So you can mold that terrain to your advantage and use it to outwit your enemies.

Dunebound Tactics was featured during Steam Next Fest, and afterward its demo was rebuilt based on player feedback. In developer Terahard Ltd.’s own words, “If you haven’t played the demo recently, it’s not the demo you remember.” You can play the new and improved demo on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/we-took-that-trip-key-art-1787602371901.png
We Took That Trip

Quite a tonal departure from the first two entries on this list, We Took That Trip from developer Lucito Loquito is a calm and relaxing road trip game. There are no timers or deadlines, no great quest that needs to be completed. It’s just you and your cat traveling in a van and meeting new people.

There are three game modes to choose from: Story, Zen, and Background. Story Mode tells a heartwarming tale of friendship, loss, and reunion. Zen is just about the vibe, going for a ride with no real goal in mind. And Background is an AFK mode that takes care of the driving for you, so you can just enjoy the visuals and lo-fi soundtrack.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/we-took-that-trip-screenshot-1787602371901.png

Each trip is procedurally generated and lasts as long as you choose, so every trip is different. There are points of interest scattered across your route, like gas stations, stores, and lookout towers, where you’ll meet people and hear their stories. But the focus is always the road and your Microbus, which you customize both the interior and exterior of with paint, stickers, and other decorations.
If you’re looking for a peaceful way to de-stress after a long day, you can check out the demo on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/cozy-builder-key-art-1787602371900.png
Cozy Builder

The peaceful vibes continue with the aptly named Cozy Builder, a sandbox building sim from Pangea Game Studios where you’ll start from scratch and restore Vineyard Valley to its former glory. You’ll use modular architectural pieces to create your château and harvest grapes, herbs, and wildflowers to create your own wines and other goods to share with the townsfolk or sell to continue funding your château.

There are tons of customization options for your château, including a variety of artwork and furniture for the interior and gardens, terraces, and greenhouses for the exterior. You can connect the greenhouse to your home, giving you a place to nurture flowers and collect rare plants.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/cozy-builder-screenshot-1787602371900.jpg

You can do all of this solo or build a shared space with your friends in multiplayer, giving each of you the chance to show off your creativity. The demo has been getting updated throughout the summer to add new features, like one-click item moving in destruct mode and full key rebinding. You can try it out for yourself on Steam .
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/mayday-the-survival-island-key-art-1787602371901.png
Mayday: The Survival Island

This open-world survival crafting game from developer Pequi Studios sees you wake up alone on an island after a mysterious crash. You’re injured, disoriented, and surrounded by untamed wilderness, so you’ll have to find a way to sustain yourself and survive. To do that, you’ll need to gather resources, craft tools, hunt wild animals, catch fish, grow crops, and build a homestead that can sustain you while you try to figure out what happened to you.

As it turns out, the island you washed up on is one of 24 that make up an archipelago, and your adventure will take you to all of them, each of which has different environments, resources, and hidden treasures. So you’ll need to continuously upgrade your tools and figure out how to adapt to each island’s challenges.

There aren’t any timed objectives or linear paths, so you decide the pace at which the story unfolds. If you want to spend hours building up your base, raising animals, and tending crops, you can do that. Or you can just find what you need to keep surviving and move on to the next part of the story, it’s up to you.

That story of Mayday: The Survival Island is focused on the mysteries of the island and how you ended up there. You’ll find strange symbols, magical totems, and fragments of a lost civilization that hint these islands are more than meets the eye. And the more you explore, the more you’ll question if ending up here was an accident and if escape is even possible. You can get a taste of all this with the free Steam demo .
